question: What is the primary function of the TSSU in a healthcare facility?

options.B: Washing bed linens for the surgical wards

explanation: The TSSU is specifically designed to handle the cleaning, sterilization, and distribution of surgical instruments and medical devices. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is the TSSU considered critical for surgical patient safety?

options.A: It ensures nurses arrive on time for their theatre shifts
options.B: It prevents contaminated tools from entering the operating room
options.C: It speeds up the overall duration of surgical procedures
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing new surgical tools

explanation: Properly sterilized equipment stops pathogens from reaching the sterile surgical site, directly preventing hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which zone in the TSSU receives dirty instruments from the operating theatre?
explanation: All used and contaminated items are first received in the decontamination zone for washing and disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: Air pressure in the decontamination zone is kept lower than surrounding areas to achieve what purpose?

options.A: Dry the washed instruments without using electricity
options.B: Prevent contaminated air from escaping into clean zones
options.C: Keep the room cool for staff working in protective gear
options.D: Ensure steam sterilizers heat up much faster

explanation: Negative pressure ensures that air flows inward into the dirty zone rather than blowing outwards into clean packaging areas. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the decontamination phase in the TSSU?

options.A: Removing organic soil and bioburden from instruments
options.B: Packaging items for long-term shelf storage
options.C: Melting down broken metal parts for recycling
options.D: Applying chemical seals to prevent rusting

explanation: Decontamination physically removes blood, tissue, and other organic matter so that sterilization can work effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why must organic debris be completely removed before sterilization takes place?

options.A: It changes the color of the external chemical indicators
options.B: It makes the instrument handles too slippery to hold
options.C: It causes the autoclave machine to rust prematurely
options.D: It can shield trapped microorganisms from the sterilizing agent

explanation: Residual blood or tissue creates a barrier that protects bacteria and spores from coming into contact with steam or chemicals. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: What action must staff perform during the inspection stage of instrument processing?

options.A: Submerge the dry instruments in an enzymatic bath
options.B: Apply industrial grease to all moving mechanical joints
options.C: Check for damage, cleanliness, and proper functioning
options.D: Wrap the items tightly in ordinary polythene bags

explanation: Inspection ensures instruments are clean, functional, and free from cracks or dull edges before being packed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which property is most essential for a surgical instrument packaging material?

options.A: Being completely transparent on both top and bottom layers
options.B: Reflecting heat away from the contents inside the autoclave
options.C: Dissolving safely inside the patient during the operation
options.D: Allowing sterilizing agent penetration while maintaining sterility

explanation: The wrapper must let steam or gas enter during the cycle, yet block microbes completely afterward during storage. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which sterilization method is considered the standard choice for most metal surgical instruments?

options.D: Boiling in water for ten minutes

explanation: Autoclaving is fast, reliable, cost-effective, and safe for most standard surgical metals. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: What do biological indicators use to test the effectiveness of a sterilization cycle?
explanation: Biological indicators contain highly resistant live bacterial spores that must be completely destroyed to prove the cycle worked. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: What inventory principle should staff use when arranging sterile packs on storage shelves?
explanation: FIFO ensures that older sterile packs are used before newly sterilized items, preventing stock from expiring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why should sterile storage areas maintain positive air pressure relative to corridors?

options.A: To help the packaged instruments dry out even further
options.B: To prevent dust and unsterile air from flowing inside
options.C: To make it easier for nursing staff to open heavy doors
options.D: To cool down the electronic inventory tracking computers

explanation: Positive pressure pushes air outward when doors open, blocking dust and airborne microbes from entering the sterile storage zone. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which item of PPE is most appropriate for staff working in the decontamination zone?

options.A: Standard cloth cap and paper mask

explanation: Decontamination workers need protection against splashing contaminated water, blood, and harsh chemicals. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for enforcing strict safety protocols in the TSSU?

options.A: Protecting staff from biological, chemical, and physical hazards
options.B: Reducing the amount of electricity consumed by autoclave machines
options.C: Ensuring that tray assembly takes the exact same time every shift
options.D: Complying with hospital policies without slowing down production

explanation: TSSU workers face hazards like sharps injuries, chemical burns, and infections, making safety protocols vital for occupational health. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)
